sml_orders.caveat: An SML order is not a CFPB complaint and is not a quality ranking. Exact NMLS is required for adverse profile attachment. 1,488-class name-only rows stay at statewide regulatory-event grain. Native Title of Order values are not collapsed. Penalty mentions are not consumer-loss amounts. CSV clock is the file update date, not current NMLS authority.

programs.application_path: TDHCA and TSAHC do not replace a mortgage underwriting decision. Buyers apply through a participating lender. Program participation is not a Texas license.

items.name: My First Texas Home
items.agency: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
items.assistance: 30-year low-interest first mortgage with down-payment and closing-cost assistance
items.maximum: Official product page: flexible DPA at 2%, 3%, 4%, and 5% of the loan amount; 30-year 0% interest second lien; 3-year forgivable second lien available. Matrix PDF dated 2026-08-17 is the fee/overlay clock.
items.eligibility: First-time homebuyers and qualified veterans. Official page notes certain first-time-buyer exceptions in targeted areas and for qualified veterans. Homebuyer education is required for TDHCA Homebuyer Program assistance.
items.income_purchase_limits: Income and purchase-price limits apply; confirm current limits on official TDHCA materials. Not restated here as a single statewide dollar cap.
items.status: Documented on official TDHCA Welcome Home pages retrieved this snapshot.
items.source_date: Official page retrieval 2026-09-04; program matrix PDF dated 2026-08-17

items.name: My Choice Texas Home
items.agency: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
items.assistance: 30-year low-interest first mortgage with down-payment and closing-cost assistance for buyers who are not limited to first-time status
items.maximum: Same official DPA family as My First Texas Home (percentage-of-loan assistance). Confirm current rate/DPA options with a participating lender.
items.eligibility: Official programs page: you do not have to be a first-time homebuyer to qualify. Homebuyer education is required for TDHCA Homebuyer Program assistance.
items.income_purchase_limits: Income and purchase-price limits apply; confirm on official TDHCA materials.
items.status: Documented on official TDHCA Welcome Home pages retrieved this snapshot.

items.name: Texas Mortgage Credit Certificate (MCC)
items.agency: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
items.assistance: Federal mortgage credit certificate that reduces federal income-tax liability dollar-for-dollar, as described on the official TDHCA page
items.maximum: Official programs page: available to veterans and first-time homebuyers with a first mortgage through the program, and as a stand-alone option. Supplies are limited.
items.eligibility: First-time homebuyers and veterans as stated on the official page. No minimum credit score with the stand-alone option, per the official programs page. Not a cash down-payment grant.
items.income_purchase_limits: MCC income/purchase rules are program-specific; confirm on the official MCC page.
items.status: Documented on official TDHCA Welcome Home pages retrieved this snapshot. Limited supply is an official statement, not a TrustHub scarcity ranking.

items.name: Texas Statewide Homebuyer Education Program (TSHEP)
items.agency: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
items.assistance: Required homebuyer education course for TDHCA Homebuyer Program assistance
items.eligibility: Completing an approved homebuyer education course is required to qualify for assistance through The TDHCA Homebuyer Program, per the official programs page.
items.status: Documented on official TDHCA Welcome Home pages retrieved this snapshot.

items.name: Homes for Texas Heroes
items.assistance: 30-year fixed-rate mortgage with down-payment assistance for eligible hero professions
items.maximum: Official TSAHC pages: DPA 3% to 5% of the loan amount, as a grant that does not have to be repaid or a 3-year deferred forgivable second lien.
items.eligibility: Official page: professional educators (including specified public-school roles), fire fighters and EMS personnel, police and correctional officers, and veterans. First-time buyer status is not required. Apply through a participating lender after the eligibility quiz.
items.income_purchase_limits: Income limits apply and can be higher in targeted areas; confirm current AMFI tables on TSAHC materials.
items.status: Documented on official TSAHC pages retrieved this snapshot.

items.name: Home Sweet Texas Home Loan Program
items.assistance: 30-year fixed-rate mortgage with down-payment assistance for eligible Texas homebuyers who do not have to qualify under the Heroes occupation list
items.maximum: Official TSAHC pages: DPA 3% to 5% of the loan amount as a grant or 3-year deferred forgivable second lien. Credit scores as low as 620 are described on the official home-buyer programs page.
items.eligibility: Low- and moderate-income Texas homebuyers as published by TSAHC. First-time buyer status is not required for DPA. First-time buyers may also research TSAHC MCC.
items.income_purchase_limits: Income and purchase-price limits apply; targeted-area limits may differ. Confirm on official TSAHC tables.
items.status: Documented on official TSAHC pages retrieved this snapshot.

items.name: TSAHC Mortgage Credit Certificate
items.assistance: Mortgage credit certificate tax credit for eligible first-time buyers, as described on official TSAHC pages
items.maximum: Official TSAHC down-payment page: first-time buyers can also apply for an MCC. Confirm current combination rules on official TSAHC guidelines; do not treat MCC as cash DPA.
items.eligibility: First-time homebuyers as stated by TSAHC. Eligibility is not guaranteed approval.
items.income_purchase_limits: MCC income limits follow the official TSAHC/federal MCC tables, which can differ from DPA AMFI tables.
items.status: Documented on official TSAHC pages retrieved this snapshot.

programs.caveat: Program terms change. Eligibility is not guaranteed approval. Headline amounts are official-page formulas, not a promise of funds. County or city local DPA is not inventoried here.

approved_lenders.caveat: No easy structured or HTML lender directory with reusable rows was acquired. TDHCA/TSAHC participating-lender search/onboarding pages are not a bulk roster. Program participation is not a license. NMLS IDs were not manufactured. Zero directory rows here means SOURCE_NOT_ACQUIRED, not an empty lender market.
approved_lenders.publication_note: Do not display directory_rows=0 as a market finding.

live_roster.caveat: Missing live roster is unknown, not zero. Do not display a fake current license count. The 2024 SML report entity count is a dated snapshot, not this live denominator.

occc.caveat: OCCC regulates overlapping consumer-credit classes such as property-tax lending and manufactured housing. That is not the SML mortgage-company roster and is not displayed as a Texas mortgage-license count.

cfpb.caveat: Complaint is not a violation. Raw complaint count is not a quality ranking and is not exposure-normalized. No company complaint rate is published without an exposure denominator.

top_issues.key: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage

cfpb.canonical_company_snapshot: National CFPB company snapshot exists separately; this overlay is statewide Texas geography and is not a company ranking.
cfpb.subproduct_note: Texas Mortgage issue buckets were acquired from the filtered CFPB API. Default unfiltered product aggregations are omitted because they are not a Texas-mortgage-only composition.

servicing.sml_servicer_registration: SML registers residential mortgage loan servicers; the 2024 report includes a dated servicer-entity count. That is not a loan-level statewide servicing file.
servicing.caveat: No easy statewide servicing performance report was acquired. Existing LenderTrustHub servicing architecture is not a Texas foreclosure portal.

foreclosure.note: No county clerk or foreclosure-posting crawl was performed. Missing statewide foreclosure structure is unknown, not zero.

public_contacts.policy: Official/public business sources only. No internet enrichment. No person contact information.
public_contacts.sml_orders_contact_note: SML enforcement CSV has no phone, email, website, or address fields.
public_contacts.caveat: Zero contact fields from an unacquired directory is a coverage gap, not a finding that Texas lenders have no phones.

regulator_matrix.what: Institution that filed HMDA loan/application records for Texas property location
regulator_matrix.proves: Reported application/origination activity in this vintage
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: Texas mortgage license, current NMLS authority, or program participation

regulator_matrix.what: Nationwide Multistate Licensing System identifier when source-native
regulator_matrix.regulator: NMLS (system of record display; not a Texas regulator)
regulator_matrix.proves: A stable identifier when printed by the source
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: Current Texas authority by itself, or whether the ID is an institution, branch, or person

regulator_matrix.what: Mortgage company, mortgage banker, mortgage servicer, wrap lender, or independent contractor processor/underwriter company under Texas SML
regulator_matrix.regulator: Texas Department of Savings and Mortgage Lending
regulator_matrix.proves: SML licensing/registration class as of a stated evidence clock
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: HMDA reporter status, OCCC authority, or TDHCA/TSAHC program participation

regulator_matrix.what: Texas Office of Consumer Credit Commissioner authority in overlapping consumer-credit classes such as property-tax lending or manufactured housing
regulator_matrix.regulator: Texas Office of Consumer Credit Commissioner
regulator_matrix.proves: OCCC authority as of that source clock when acquired

regulator_matrix.what: Individual residential mortgage loan originator licensed through NMLS and sponsored by an SML or OCCC company as applicable
regulator_matrix.regulator: Texas SML or Texas OCCC via NMLS display
regulator_matrix.proves: Individual originator credential path when source-native
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: A company license, and this site does not publish an MLO person directory

regulator_matrix.what: Bank, savings bank, or credit union operating under a prudential charter rather than an SML mortgage-company license alone
regulator_matrix.regulator: Federal and/or Texas Department of Banking / SML savings-bank supervision as applicable
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: SML mortgage-company license or HMDA completeness

regulator_matrix.what: Appears on a TDHCA or TSAHC participating-lender path for one or more homebuyer programs
regulator_matrix.proves: Program-participation listing as of directory/page retrieval
regulator_matrix.does_not_prove: Texas license, endorsement, or TrustHub recommendation

gaps: No current complete Texas mortgage-company bulk roster was acquired. Live licensed-company denominator is UNKNOWN, not zero.
Complete MLO / RMLO person universe is not published and was not scraped from NMLS.
Name-only SML orders cannot be attached to lender profiles. Not every enforcement order has an exact NMLS ID.
SML CSV NMLS IDs are not source-typed as institution vs person vs branch.
NMLS Consumer Access remains search-only. Not scraped.
No easy structured TDHCA/TSAHC participating-lender directory was acquired.
No easy statewide OCCC mortgage-company roster was acquired.
No easy statewide servicing performance report was acquired.
Company-level CFPB complaint exposure denominators are not computed.
The 2024 SML report entity count is dated October 31, 2024, and is not a live roster.

EXACT: NMLS when source-native on the SML order row
identity_rules.HIGH_CONFIDENCE: exact legal name + exact official business address for non-adverse descriptive data only
identity_rules.REVIEW_REQUIRED: program lender names without source-native NMLS
identity_rules.UNSAFE: name-only SML orders — not used for adverse profile attachment

semantic_guardrails: HMDA is not a license roster
HMDA reporter is not a Texas licensee
NMLS ID is not current Texas authority by itself
State order is not a complaint
Denial rate is not quality and is not a discrimination finding
Program participation is not an endorsement or a license
Name-only order is not safe profile attachment
Penalty amount is not consumer loss
